The week, in one breath

183.7 points of pure opening-day violence

Opening week arrived with a detonation. The Pirates of the CaribBijan hung 183.7 on Steven diggs — the highest score the league has seen — behind D'Andre Swift (31.9), Bijan Robinson (27.3) and Jaxson Dart (26.6). At the other end of the universe, lotes started three players who scored exactly 0.0 and a quarterback who managed 0.52, finishing with 49.22 and the season's first public apology tour.

And before the confetti even settled, the wire moved: Caleb Williams and Tetairoa McMillan went to Kings of New York, Lamar Jackson and DJ Moore to Steven diggs, in the blockbuster that will define somebody's season. Williams celebrated his new address with a league-best 37.26.

Game Stories

Every matchup gets a case file, a culprit and one completely imagined quote.
Blowout

The Pirates hang 183.7 and call it a warning

Pirates of the CaribBijan def. Steven diggs | 183.7 – 119.06

Pirates · 1–0BY 64.64Steven · 0–1

D'Andre Swift (31.9), Bijan Robinson (27.3) and Jaxson Dart (26.6) all cleared 26 in the same lineup, and the Pirates hung 183.7 — the biggest number this league has produced — in the season opener. Three different players could have headlined three different teams' weeks. They were all wearing one jersey.

Steven diggs did nothing wrong. David Montgomery posted 27.4, Lamar Jackson 24.96 and DJ Moore 18.5, and the club still lost by 64.64 — the league's biggest margin. Kyle Pitts' 0.0 was the only blemish, and it wouldn't have mattered if he'd scored 30.

“We scored 119 and lost by 64. Frame the week and hang it in a museum of cruelty.”Imagined postgame quote · Steven diggs
Comedy

lotes starts three ghosts and a rumor at QB

The CMC def. lotes | 104.7 – 49.22

CMC · 1–0BY 55.48lotes · 0–1

The forensic report: Odell Beckham 0.0, Jordan Addison 0.0, Colston Loveland 0.0, and quarterback Sam Darnold 0.52. Four starters combined for barely half a point. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 22.2 did heroic, unrewarded work — nearly half of lotes' entire 49.22 — while Omarion Hampton (8.3) and Jameson Williams (6.5) rounded out a lineup that read like a cry for help.

The CMC needed only competence: Trey McBride (20.0), Dak Prescott (15.4) and Jordan Mason (11.9) carried a 104.7 that would have lost to nine other teams this week. Against lotes, it was a 55.48-point coronation.

“Three zeros and a half-point quarterback. We didn't field a team, we fielded a rumor.”Imagined postgame quote · lotes
Game Recap

Jeanty announces himself; Mommas Home rolls

Mommas Home <3 def. Everybody Hurts | 146.8 – 115.12

Mommas · 1–0BY 31.68Hurts · 0–1

Ashton Jeanty (29.7), Trevor Lawrence (26.1) and Chuba Hubbard (22.2) stacked 78 points between them, and Mommas Home <3 cruised to 146.8 — a score that beats every team in the league except the Pirates' fireworks show.

Everybody Hurts was respectable in defeat: Jalen Hurts scored 24.72, Jonathan Taylor 23.6 and Juwan Johnson 12.9. A 115.12 opener wins plenty of weeks. It does not win this one.

“Second-highest score in the league and nobody's talking about us. Good. Stay asleep.”Imagined postgame quote · Mommas Home <3
Thriller

Caleb vs. Allen: the QB duel of the week

Kings of New York def. Romo's Rum Runner | 125.16 – 116.66

Kings · 1–0BY 8.5Romo · 0–1

The two best quarterback performances in the league collided in one matchup. Caleb Williams, freshly traded to Kings of New York, posted a league-best 37.26; Josh Allen answered with 35.66 for Romo's Rum Runner. Derrick Henry's 34.8 and Amon-Ra St. Brown's 23.7 gave the Kings the deeper bench of stars, and that was the 8.5-point difference.

Romo's got 31.1 from Jahmyr Gibbs and only 12.0 from Rhamondre Stevenson beyond that. The Kings even survived starting the Houston Texans defense, which scored −1.0. When your defense scores negative and you still win the week's closest game, your quarterback did something historic.

“Thirty-seven points in a new uniform, week one. The trade paperwork is already framed.”Imagined postgame quote · Kings of New York
Shootout

A 265-point track meet, settled by depth

J9hunna def. dellnuts | 139.34 – 125.76

J9hunna · 1–0BY 13.58dellnuts · 0–1

Christian Watson (29.7), Dallas Goedert (21.7) and Breece Hall (18.8) powered J9hunna to 139.34 — and it still wasn't comfortable, because dellnuts brought Justin Jefferson (27.2), Bucky Irving (16.8) and Ladd McConkey (16.7) to the same fight.

The strangest line of the shootout belongs to the winner: Jaylen Waddle scored 0.7 for J9hunna — a goose-adjacent line in a game his team won by double digits. Depth covered for him. dellnuts' 125.76 is the highest losing score of the week — a silver medal nobody asked for.

“Scored 125 and lost. Somebody check whether the schedule is a prank.”Imagined postgame quote · dellnuts
Game Recap

Walker's 32.6 masterpiece, framed and wasted

Honk Dawgs def. lexxyfour | 107.76 – 94.82

Honk · 1–0BY 12.94lexxy · 0–1

Honk Dawgs won the professional way: Chris Olave (23.2), Joe Burrow (15.16) and Cam Skattebo (14.1) built a steady 107.76 with no single explosion required. Boring, balanced, 1–0.

lexxyfour had the week's fourth-best player and lost anyway. Kenneth Walker's 32.6 towered over Kyren Williams (14.0) and Drake Maye (12.82), and then the floor gave out — Romeo Doubs posted 0.0, a full goose egg in a 12.94-point loss. One star, one zero, one long season opener.

“Walker gave us 32 and we gave him a loss. We owe that man an apology and a supporting cast.”Imagined postgame quote · lexxyfour
Fraud Watch · Case file

Pirates of the CaribBijan

Subject: one 183.7-point explosion. Status: unsustainable until proven otherwise.

Nobody is accusing the Pirates of cheating. We are accusing them of peaking in Week 1. Three starters — Swift (31.9), Bijan (27.3) and Dart (26.6) — all posted top-12 scores in the league in the same lineup, in the same week. That is not a roster construction. That is a solar eclipse.

The gap tells the story: the league's second-best score was 146.8. The Pirates beat it by 36.9 points and beat their own opponent by 64.64 despite Steven diggs posting a perfectly respectable 119.06. Fraud Watch's position is simple: do it again. Until then, 183.7 is a fireworks show, not a dynasty.

Honorable mention in the getaway-car division: The CMC is 1–0 with 104.7 points — the lowest winning score of the week — because lotes fielded three zeros and a 0.52 quarterback. Some wins you earn. Some wins are left on your doorstep.

183.7 · Do It Again

Fraud Watch verdict: spectacular, and deeply suspicious.
